newsitem.title: ANGOLA: UNITA generals fly to Luanda for army integration.
newsitem.headline: UNITA generals fly to Luanda for army integration.

text.p: The military chief of Angola's former rebel UNITA movement and four of his generals arrived in Luanda on Monday for integration into a single national army, after almost two years of peace negotiations.

General Arlindo Chenda Ben Ben and another top general, Domingos Wiyo, were flown from UNITA's central highlands headquarters in Bailundo to the government-controlled capital in a United Nations aircraft.
The three other generals Julio Lopes Tchipa, Jeronimo Jorge Regresso and Felisberto Ngele, arrived together on a private charter aircraft.

Their planes followed minutes behind that of the U.N. special envoy to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, who was summoned by UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi earlier on Monday to fetch the generals from UNITA's bush headquarters.
"Today is a very important day for the peace process," Beye told reporters at the U.N.'s hangar at Luanda Airport soon after their arrival.
The generals were met by one of the government's negotiators, Higino Carneiro, U.N. military head Phillip Sibanda and officials from the three observer countries America, Portugal and Russia.
Savimbi pledged at a meeting with Beye last Thursday to fulfil new commitments within 10 days to make progress on political and military issues stalling the peace process.
He also promised to begin sending his top nine generals to Luanda before September 20 for integration into a single army, ahead of a leaders' summit later this month.

Ben Ben, who travelled with his wife and two sons, told reporters: "Our return is in compliance with the Lusaka Protocol (peace plan). We would like to open ways to better understand some aspects that are still not clear.
"We came here for the integration process into the Angolan Armed Forces (FAA). We are going to hear from the FAA which are the steps we should be following (for integration)."
Ben Ben was last in Luanda in 1995 for military discussions with the Angolan government but left the city shortly after one of his security guards was shot and wounded at his home.

The security of UNITA's generals in the capital has been one of the most contentious issues in negotiations ahead of their return to Luanda. Independent military observers said at least one of the top generals had recently received death threats.
The generals were staying in a top Luanda hotel for the night, heavily guarded by a special police unit.
Ben Ben said the rest of UNITA's generals would arrive shortly, but gave no date.
Carneiro welcomed their arrival as a key step towards peace, saying: "This is an important step, a step for which we have waited for a long time."
